structuredContent.governing_intent: Revise Pre-Python architecture/work-unit documentation only to reconcile candidate contracts with the superseding Founder FD-01 ownership split: external work-management providers remain canonical for upstream product/work-management state, while AlienIntent becomes canonical for execution-control state after explicit release of a READY BIU. No source, tests, runtime configuration, services, GitHub state, FactoryChecks, Python implementation, or EOS edits are authorized.
structuredContent.summary: The supplied work packet has clear governing authority, scope boundaries, and observable acceptance criteria. It is a cohesive documentation consistency update driven by one Founder decision, not a set of independent feature decisions. The work may require engineering/documentation research to locate all affected sections and preserve provenance, but no material owner intent appears unresolved.
implementation_unknowns: Exact current contents and cross-links of the affected docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/*.md files are not provided and would need to be inspected during implementation.
The exact format and location conventions for assessment/review receipts and docs/work-units/pre-python-gate packets must be followed from the repository during implementation.

The specific set of sections requiring edits across product intent, domain model, work/release, ACL, event ingress, persistence, control plane, configuration, scheduling, context/evidence, conformance, Founder-decision registers, reconciliation, gate report, matrix, execution, and validation must be identified from the existing documents.
The documentation checker, link/coverage/scope checks, and independent delta review process are referenced but their exact commands or manual procedures are not specified in the packet.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through document diffs and review receipts: the six-point FD-01 decision must be recorded with supersession, upstream product authority and internal execution authority must be distinguished consistently, exact release/idempotency/projection/immutability/profile/vendor/persistence/boundary/conformance/gate-row semantics must be reflected, prohibited file categories must remain untouched, prior authority and receipts must be preserved, and link/coverage/scope plus independent delta review can provide one meaningful verification verdict. No runtime execution is needed because the authorized work is documentation-only.
material_risks: Accidentally converting candidate contract text into approved architecture beyond the specific Founder FD-01 ownership decision.
Over-copying Node whole-lifecycle authority into Python candidate contracts instead of preserving only relevant conformance evidence and unchanged Node bootstrap behavior.
Introducing an unauthorized mandatory human release requirement despite the existing automatic-release ON/OFF policy.
Blurring upstream product authority with AlienIntent execution authority, especially around imported views, projections, post-release edits, and DONE/closure state.
Silently approving or closing remaining Founder decisions other than FD01.
Changing source, tests, configuration, service behavior, GitHub state, FactoryChecks, EOS materials, or Python implementation despite the documentation-only scope.
Failing to preserve provenance, historical manifests, prior assessment receipts, or supersession links while reconciling the documents.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed with a documentation-only implementation against the supplied Founder decision and scope constraints, then perform the specified local documentation/link/coverage/scope checks and obtain an independent delta review before a meaningful local commit with no push.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the material owner decision that previously blocked contract reconciliation is explicitly supplied and supersedes older alternatives. The requested changes are semantically unified around one ownership split, with clear exclusions and observable documentation acceptance criteria. Remaining uncertainty is implementation research about existing document structure and verification mechanics, not unresolved product, architecture, policy, or authority intent. There is no supplied evidence of an unavailable prerequisite or incompatible competing ownership that would require HOLD, and no independent decision centers requiring SPLIT.
